findings.reason: isUnknownOption (lines 972-989) returns true for an argument like 'command' because every pattern it checks is anchored on ^-. With unknown-options-as-args on, line 225 now catches the argument, pushes it and carries on, and the halt-at-non-option break at lines 397-399 is never reached. Trigger: ['command','--foo'] with both options on now gives foo:true instead of passing '--foo' through.
findings.claim: Removing the `/^-/` guard means that when unknown-options-as-args is on, every non-dash positional goes through pushPositional at line 225. halt-at-non-option at line 397 never fires, so flags that come after a positional get parsed as options.
findings.evidence: The diff changes line 225 from `if (arg !== '--' && /^-/.test(arg) && isUnknownOptionAsArg(arg))` to `if (arg !== '--' && isUnknownOptionAsArg(arg))`. `isUnknownOption` (lines 972-990) returns `!hasFlagsMatching(...)`, and every pattern it checks is anchored on a leading dash (`/^-+.../`, and `negatedBoolean` is `^--no-`). So for an argument like `./file.js` no pattern matches and the function returns true. That argument then hits `pushPositional(arg)` at line 226 and the loop continues. The `else if (configuration['halt-at-non-option']) { notFlags = args.slice(i); break }` branch at lines 397-399 is never reached. Trigger: `parser(['--foo','./file.js','--bar'], {configuration:{'unknown-options-as-args':true,'halt-at-non-option':true}, boolean:['foo','bar']})` used to give `_: ['./file.js','--bar']`. It now gives `_: ['./file.js']` with `bar: true`. No test in test/yargs-parser.cjs combines the two options: the halt-at-non-option tests at lines 2980-3010 don't set unknown-options-as-args.

findings.reason: For non-dash arguments, hasAllShortFlags (line 946) returns early, and every pattern in isUnknownOption is anchored on ^-+, so each regex fails on the first character. Any perf cost is trivial. The behaviour problem with the deleted guard is already covered by C1/X1. Lowered from medium.
findings.claim: Removing the guard may undo the #394 perf fix by sending positionals through the regex checks.
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:42 records `perf: address slow parse when using unknown-options-as-args (#394)`. The guard keeps `isUnknownOption`, with its six regex checks and `hasAllShortFlags`, from running on arguments that don't start with a dash. The diff only removes the guard and adds no test. acceptance.md just points to story.md and tests.lock, and neither file is in the export. The perf tests at test/yargs-parser.cjs:3989-4004 only try dash-leading strings, so they would not catch a slowdown on long non-dash positionals.
